record.context_brief: First polynomial class and its discrete versions
record.original_question: For the four-parameter orthogonal polynomial H_n(z; μ, ν, α, θ) on the real line, together with the two discrete versions that the source denotes by h_n(k; μ, ν, α, β) and g_n(k; μ, ν, β, N), can one derive a full analytic description from their current definition by three-term recursion relations and initial values alone? In particular, determine their weight functions, generating functions, asymptotics, orthogonality relations, Rodrigues-type formulas, forward/backward shift operator relations, zeros, and a closed-form representation, for example in terms of hypergeometric functions.

evidence.quote: Since 2005, however, we found a new class of exactly solvable problems that are associated with orthogonal polynomials, which were overlooked in the mathematics and physics literature [5-12]. These polynomials are defined, up to now, by their three-term recursion relations and initial value P_0(ε) = 1. However, their other important properties are yet to be derived analytically. These properties include the weight functions, generating functions, asymptotics, orthogonality relations, Rodrigues-type formulas, etc.

Due to the prime significance of these new (or modified) polynomials along with their discrete versions to the solution of various problems in physics and mathematics, we urge experts in the field of orthogonal polynomials to study them, derive their analytic properties and write them in closed form (e.g., in terms of hypergeometric functions). The sought-after properties of these polynomials include the weight functions, generating functions, asymptotics, orthogonality relations, Rodrigues-type formulas, Forward/Backward shift operator relations, zeros, etc.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the following three families of polynomials, each defined solely by a three-term recurrence relation together with the initial value P_0 = 1.

(A) A continuous four-parameter family { H_n(z; μ, ν, α, θ) }_{n=0}^{∞} of polynomials in a real variable z ∈ ℝ, depending on real parameters μ, ν, α, θ (with the parameter ranges that make the recursion produce a positive-definite moment problem on the real line).

(B) A discrete four-parameter family { h_n(k; μ, ν, α, β) }_{n=0}^{∞} of polynomials in the discrete variable k ∈ {0, 1, 2, …}, again specified by a three-term recurrence and h_0 ≡ 1 (countably infinite spectrum case).

(C) A finite discrete four-parameter family { g_n(k; μ, ν, β, N) }_{n=0}^{N} in the variable k ∈ {0, 1, …, N}, specified by a three-term recurrence and g_0 ≡ 1 (finite spectrum case of size N+1).

In each of the three cases, the recurrence coefficients are explicit rational/algebraic functions of n and the parameters (assumed given), and the recursion alone determines the polynomials.

Problem. Starting only from the three-term recurrence relations and initial conditions defining H_n, h_n, and g_n, derive a complete analytic description of these polynomials. In particular:

1. Determine the orthogonality measure / weight function for each family (continuous weight on ℝ for H_n, discrete weights with countably infinite or finite support for h_n and g_n, respectively), and prove the corresponding orthogonality relations.
2. Obtain a generating function for each family.
3. Derive the asymptotic behavior of the polynomials as n → ∞ (and, where relevant, as the variable tends to infinity).
4. Establish a Rodrigues-type formula expressing the n-th polynomial via a finite-difference or differential operator applied to the weight.
5. Find forward and backward shift operator relations linking the polynomials of degree n and n ± 1 with shifted parameters.
6. Describe the location and properties of the zeros.
7. Obtain a closed-form representation, for example as a (possibly terminating) generalized hypergeometric series _pF_q or basic hypergeometric series.

Provide such a complete analytic theory, or prove obstructions explaining why some of these objects cannot be expressed in standard closed form.
artifact.status_search_result: No published work was found that supplies a complete analytic theory (weight, generating function, Rodrigues formula, shift operators, closed-form hypergeometric representation) for these polynomials. The families remain primarily defined through their three-term recursions in the available literature, and the call for experts to derive these properties does not appear to have been answered in full. Partial progress on related Alhaidari-type polynomial families exists, but a comprehensive solution for H_n, h_n, and g_n has not been verified.

status_evidence.title: Open problem in orthogonal polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: Polynomials defined by three-term recursion relations and initial values P_0 = 1; weight functions, generating functions, asymptotics, orthogonality relations, Rodrigues-type formulas, etc., are yet to be derived analytically.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is posed as open, with the analytic properties of these polynomial families not yet derived.

status_evidence.title: Quantum mechanics with orthogonal polynomials (Alhaidari)
status_evidence.snippet: A new class of orthogonal polynomials with continuous spectrum on the real line and two discrete versions, defined by their recursions.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work continues to define these polynomials by recursion, indicating the analytic theory remains incomplete.
